name: Abstract vs. Concrete Oscillations
description: Evaluates the transition rhythm between high-level theories and deeply grounded, sensory examples.
mechanism: Human storytelling and persuasive writing generally follow a strict 'accordion' pattern: making a broad abstract statement, instantly followed by a violent grounding into concrete reality (e.g., 'Justice is flawed; consider the broken gavel at the courthouse'). Modern RLHF-trained AI struggles profoundly with this oscillation. It prefers to remain safely suspended in the abstract macro-layer to avoid hallucinating incorrect specific facts. This tool measures the delta and transition speed between abstract sentences and concrete, physically-grounded sentences. A flatline remaining entirely in the safety of abstraction, with no sudden drops into hyper-specific sensory details, is a massive algorithmic red flag.
parameters:
Analysis: Sentence-Level Grounding Variance
Metric: Oscillation Amplitude & Frequency
Output: 0-100 Reality-Grounding Deficit Score
accuracy: High — 80-87%, particularly lethal against AI essays attempting to mimic investigative journalism or personal narratives.
source: Psycholinguistics and NLP text abstraction analysis research.
useCase: Isolating AI texts that sound plausible but lack the unpredictable, messy real-world examples that humans use to anchor their arguments.
strengths:
• Brilliantly targets the AI's programmed fear of hallucination (which causes it to avoid committing to hyper-specific imagery).
• Measures rhythm and flow, which is vastly harder for a naive prompter to fake than mere vocabulary.
• Exceptional at discerning between real journalism and AI-spun news aggregates.
limitations:
• Hard to tune without generating false positives on inherently dry, bureaucratic government documents.
• Requires sophisticated dependency parsing to distinguish if a concrete noun is actively grounded or just part of a metaphor.
• Fails on extremely short texts where no real accordion oscillation pattern has room to form.

references.title: Brysbaert, M., et al. (2014). Concreteness ratings for 40 thousand generally known English word lemmas. Behavior Research Methods.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
